Owner→Quick Request (mobile 390) created REQ-2026-000003 (QUICK/SOURCING, RFQ-2026-000002 auto-published). Supplier UI: /supply/inbox→open→intend-btn→submit quote (₹25.50 × 100 STEM) → QTN-2026-000001; asked clarification. Buyer UI: /demand/rfqs/{id}→answered clarification→picked offer + award qty 100→AWD-2026-000001 (fullyAwarded=true, requirement→AWARDED, quote→ACCEPTED). issues: All datetime pickers use native browser <input type=datetime-local> instead of a shadcn Calendar component — inconsistent look with the rest of the dark themed UI (grayscale calendar glyph, no popover, differs across Chromium/Safari).
Quote-valid-until date input hint is very small; when user picks a past date the only feedback is a red 'validTo must be in the future' text — no inline field-level validation before submit.

Nav renders Ops desk / Admin / Catalog admin links unconditionally for every logged-in user. A plain supplier can click them and lands on a 'Missing required permission' page. Preferable to hide items the user has no permission for (permission-driven nav) to reduce dead clicks.

The pick radio + award-qty input are visually very small (~20px, no label). On the desktop shot the whole row looks near empty until you know to click the radio. Consider adding column headers 'Select' and inline placeholder text 'Award qty (max N)'.

action_items: (Optional UX) Hide Ops desk / Admin / Catalog admin nav links for users without the corresponding permission (owner=platform.admin/procurement.manage; supplier normally sees only Procurement/Inbox/Catalog/Capabilities/Account).
(Optional UX) Replace native datetime-local inputs on QuickRequestPage/EventsPage/SupplierRfqPage with a shadcn Calendar+time popover for visual consistency with the dark theme.
(Minor) Add clearer visual affordance for the award-selection radio and the award-qty input in the buyer quote-comparison table (labels, max-qty placeholder).
critical_code_review_comments: Auth middleware correctly returns 403 with details.missing=['procurement.manage'] for supplier hitting /demand/ops/desk — the frontend surfaces this as an inline 'Missing required permission' message on the Procurement desk page (no crash, no white screen). Good defense-in-depth alongside client-side hiding.

publish-rfq endpoint returns {id, ref, status:'PUBLISHED', suppliersInvited:1} — idempotent when repeat Idempotency-Key is sent (test not re-run but code path is protected by unique indexes per Build 3 guardrails).

Award endpoint returns {id, ref, fullyAwarded:true} and same-tick requirement transitions to AWARDED + quote-version to ACCEPTED — invariants (sum awarded <= requirement qty) enforced server-side; UI updates status chip immediately.
Tenant isolation confirmed: supplier org GET /api/demand/requirements/{buyer-req-id} returns 404 (not 403), matching the guardrail 'cross-org 404'.
